reason: Both fully satisfy the hard requirements (phases with percentages/entry criteria, correctly formatted RISK lines, decommissioning kept out of the final migration phase, numeric halt thresholds, and a correct PHASES line), but Response A is the more usable and rigorous plan: it adds a pre-migration shadow/parity phase to de-risk cutover, gates each sub-wave of the large ramp phase on the halt metrics rather than just the phase as a whole, specifies concrete rollback mechanics and SLAs (e.g., pointer-flip system-of-record switch, <4hr rollback for 10k accounts), and dedicates an explicit decommission phase with its own 30-day soak and sign-off criteria, giving stronger operational detail than Response B's more generic three-phase treatment.
